text:
Sam: CI on main turned red after the deps PR landed — failing on the wheel ABI/platform for cryptography during pip install. build-linux-x86_64 job shows 'ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement cryptography==40.0.1 (from -r requirements.txt (line 12))'
Anya: can you paste the failing log snippet? which job number?
Sam: job 7821. here's the pip output from the test vm:
```
Looking in indexes: https://pypi.org/simple
Collecting cryptography==40.0.1
  Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement cryptography==40.0.1 (from -r requirements.txt (line 12))
  No matching distribution found for cryptography==40.0.1
```
CI Bot: <https://ci.redwood.example/runs/7821|build #7821> failed on test matrix: linux-x86_64, python3.10, manylinux2014
Leo: suspicious — cryptography wheels often have platform tags. Did the PR change the index or the extra-index-url?
Sam: PR only bumped deps via `poetry lock` then `poetry export` -> requirements.txt. No index changes. It was green in my macOS run.
Maria: maybe the wheel for 40.0.1 wasn't published for manylinux2014/pypy? or pip is trying to pick a platform-specific wheel and failing to fall back to source because we disallow builds in CI. Any chance the build env disallows --no-binary?
Anya: good point. CI uses PIP_NO_BINARY=:all: in the build container to ensure reproducible builds. If a wheel isn't available for that platform, pip will error instead of building from sdist. Can you try removing that env and repro locally in the same container?
Sam: repro steps I used:
```bash
docker run --rm -it python:3.10-slim bash -c '\
  pip install -U pip wheel setuptools && \
  PIP_NO_BINARY= cryptography==40.0.1 || true
'
```
It fails the same.
Leo: another angle: maybe cryptography uploaded a wheel with a different tag (musllinux vs manylinux) and our builder uses musl vs glibc mismatch. Which base image do we use for linux-x86_64?
Sam: build uses our internal manylinux-based container (glibc). But the new packaging did add musl wheels for linux-musl. So if pip resolver prefers musl wheel (unlikely) that would be odd.
Maria: can someone run a quick index check from the CI machine? e.g. `pip install --no-build-isolation --no-deps --only-binary=:all: cryptography==40.0.1 -v` to see available files/pieces.
Anya: I'll spawn a debug job and run that on the same runner image, give me 10m.
(9 minutes later)
Anya: ran the debug container — output shows only a macos wheel and a musl wheel uploaded for 40.0.1, no manylinux2014 wheel for x86_64. That explains it.
Sam: ok, so our PIP_NO_BINARY policy is preventing sdist build and there's no manylinux wheel -> CI fails. Do we want to pin back to 39.x until upstream publishes the manylinux wheel?
Leo: alternative: relax PIP_NO_BINARY for that package in CI for this job (allow building from sdist) so tests can continue while we open an upstream issue with cryptography maintainers. Risk: building cryptography in CI takes longer and may need rust toolchain.
Maria: confirmed — cryptography sdist requires Rust to build new versions. Our builder doesn't have rust installed. So building from sdist will fail anyway. Pinning back is safer short-term.
Sam: I'll open a quick revert PR to pin cryptography==39.0.1 in the exported requirements and bump again after upstream publishes manylinux wheel.
Anya: also sending a bisect request — @eng-infra if anyone can help confirm whether the poetry lock step changed platform markers; maybe we can add a check in CI to fail-fast when a dependency lacks a compatible wheel.
Leo: +1 to bisect. I can take a look tomorrow morning, but pin revert sounds good for now.
CI Bot: build #7821 rerun triggered by Sam (build #7822)
Sam: rerun failed (same error) so I'll cut the revert PR now.
Maria: thanks — please add a short note in the PR description referencing this thread and the CI job link.
Sam: done, PR opened: <https://git.example/redwood/infra/pull/560> — pinning cryptography to 39.0.1.
Anya: thanks. closing loop once #560 merges and build goes green. :thumbsup:
